Jonas, Priyom —

As we finalize the mutual action plan for our pilot with MedLabs, procurement asked for a short write-up of the unit-econ assumptions that will govern acceptance gates. They specifically want: tokens per request, sample latency under expected QPS, and caching/batching assumptions that could materially change cost.

We pulled together a very rough traffic profile (attached) and would appreciate Redwood’s expected tokens/$ numbers and any recommendations on caching thresholds and batching window settings. We need something to attach to the MSA redline package by next Tuesday (2028-11-07).

Key asks:
- Baseline tokens per end-user interaction (we provided sample prompts in the sheet)
- Expected tokens per dollar at the pilot profile
- Recommended cache TTLs and prefix sizes for clinical note generation
- A short list of gating criteria (e.g., cost per 1k sessions > $X triggers rework)

Can you confirm whether the token econ will change materially if we enable 8-bit quantization / different model variant?

Thanks — Amir

Amir —

Appreciate the clear asks and the traffic snapshot. I pulled a quick first-pass from our pilot model run (see attached MAP sheet) — below are the highlights and open items we should resolve before we lock the MAP: 

Summary (pilot profile):
- Median tokens per session (sample prompts): ~420 tokens (prompt+response)
- Estimated tokens / $ (hosted Redwood API, x8 batch-friendly kernel): ~110k tokens per $1 at current quantized endpoint (4-bit Q8_0) for the model family we've discussed
- Enabling 8-bit/4-bit quantization moves tokens/$ by ~+15–35% depending on response length and KV-cache hit rates

Recommendations (to include in MAP):
1) Caching: enable prefix caching on the clinical-note intro + common system prompts. For your profile, a 24h TTL on stable templates and a per-patient prefix key reduced token generation by ~18% in the run.
2) Batching: configure a 20–40ms batching window for queued requests at spikes — keeps P95 latency under 400ms and improves tokens/$ materially for bursty workloads. We can tune windows per route in the Dedicated plan.
3) Fallback policy: include an explicit MAP line for automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if model-specific per-hour spend exceeds threshold X. We can provide per-model costing in the attached tab.

Open items I need from you to finalize the MAP:
- Confirm the expected concurrent active sessions (not total users) during peak 5-minute windows
- Which templates are stable vs. frequently edited (so we can recommend proper cache keys)

I’ve attached a working MAP token-econ sheet (map-token-econ-sheet.xlsx) and a short inference-profile-sample.json describing kernel/quant settings we used. Priyom / Karthik — can you add a 1-paragraph note about quantization risk (quality vs cost) and whether we recommend controlled A/B with a quality eval?

Next step: if we can get the concurrency and template list today, I’ll push an updated MAP with gating numbers by EOD tomorrow.

—Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding a few engineering specifics that are useful to call out in the MAP. Short bullets so procurement has concrete levers: 

- Batching: our runtime supports continuous batching across concurrent requests. For medlabs’ profile (median 420 tokens), moving from no batching to a 20ms batching window improved throughput ~1.6x and reduced tokens/$ by ~27% in our bench. The trade: small added jitter (10–25ms) on p50.
- KV/prefix cache: strong wins for template-driven outputs. We saw 15–22% token reduction with a per-patient prefix of the first 64 tokens and TTL=24h. If your app rewrites templates often, reduce TTL to 1h and we still get ~8% savings.
- Quantization: 4-bit Q8_0 gave the best cost uplift with minimal dev repros in our evals. However, for clinically sensitive answers we recommend an eval cohort (10k prompts) to confirm no regression. Quantization can change hallucination profile subtly — include a quality gate in MAP.
- Cost gating examples (to include as language in MAP):
  * If tokens / 1k sessions > $Y for 3 consecutive days -> initiate cost triage and rollout of caching/batch tuning.
  * If model variant A shows >2% negative delta on NPS-style quality metric vs baseline -> pause variant rollout.

I attached a tiny inference-profile snippet we used. Happy to add a one-line note for the MAP about the expected delta when switching to cheaper GPUs (if they later move to Dedicated).

On the practical side: Priyom, can you draft the gating bullets for inclusion in the MAP doc? I put suggested thresholds in the spreadsheet but we should align with sales on what’s acceptable.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime

Amir / Lia —

Thanks — the inputs above are great and I’ve consolidated everything into the MAP draft (linked). Key items we’ve captured for procurement and the MAP gating table:

1) Economic assumptions (final):
- Baseline: 420 median tokens/session -> ~110k tokens / $1 (hosted, quantized endpoint)
- With recommended caching + 20ms batching -> effective tokens / $ increases to ~140k tokens / $1 (projected ~27% improvement)
- Quantization guardrail: expected +15–35% tokens/$ uplift depending on average response length; requires a pre-release quality cohort test.

2) Gating language for MAP (for inclusion in MSA appendix):
- Cost gate: if 7-day rolling tokens per 1k sessions > $Z (value in sheet) -> trigger ops runbook + scheduled tuning cadence (48h).
- Quality gate: if model variant shows >2% regression on the MAP eval set (5k prompts) -> pause rollout and revert to previous variant.

3) Timeline:
- Today (11/03): Redwood finalizes MAP doc for attachment to MSA (I uploaded version v1)
- 11/07 EOD: MedLabs procurement submits redline + MAP appendix to legal
- 11/13: Pilot kick — initial telemetry check at 72h, gating review at 7 days

4) Next steps for MedLabs (action items):
- Confirm peak concurrent active sessions (concurrency number) — Amir to provide by COB today
- Provide list of stable templates vs. editable templates (sheet tab)
- Sign off on the gating thresholds in the sheet (I added suggested values)

We’ll include the two attachments (map-token-econ-sheet.xlsx + inference-profile-sample.json) in the package. If you give the concurrency number I’ll replace placeholder thresholds with actual per-1k-session metrics.

If everything looks good I’ll put the MAP doc in the HubSpot deal record and mark the MAP milestone as Ready for Legal.

Thanks — Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
